signature.name: Saint Sophia Cathedral
signature.detail: Harbin's most photographed landmark, a green-domed Russian Orthodox cathedral that now houses a museum of city architecture. Go early morning for fewer crowds and better light on the brick facade; it sits a short walk from the central shopping street.

signature.name: Songhua River
signature.detail: The wide river that shapes Harbin, popular for riverside walks and, in deep winter, frozen activities on the ice. Visit at sunset for the best views; the promenade is free and easy to reach from the central districts.

signature.name: Stalin Park
signature.detail: A long riverside park along the Songhua, a relaxed local spot for strolling and people-watching. Combine it with a river walk; it is free and busiest in summer evenings and during winter ice season.

signature.name: Harbin Polarland
signature.detail: A polar-themed aquarium known for its penguin and beluga displays, a good indoor option in harsh weather. Check show times before you go and allow a couple of hours; it is on the Sun Island side of the river.

signature.name: Volga Manor
signature.detail: A Russian-style park with wooden architecture and gardens outside the city center. It needs a taxi or bus ride and a half day, so go on a clear day and check opening hours in winter.

stay: Good 3-4* hotel $50-90 a night; peak festival season higher
transport: Metro about $0.5-1 a ride; taxis cheap
